title: Everything Moving Apart
question: What does it mean that the universe is expanding?
hook: From any galaxy, nearly everything else seems to run away.
idea: Distances between unbound parts of the universe grow, and there is no outside to expand into.

beats.prompt: You measure two distant galaxies. One is twice as far from you as the other. How do their speeds of moving away compare, on average?

choices.label: The farther one moves away about twice as fast
Both move away at the same speed
choices.feedback: It is tempting to think speed is a property of each galaxy, but speed grows in proportion to distance.

choices.label: The nearer one moves away faster
choices.feedback: That has it backwards: speeds are proportional to distance, so farther means faster.

beats.explain: To any observer, galaxies move away at speeds proportional to their distance, on average.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in discovering the expansion in order.
items: Slipher finds light from remote galaxies redshifted
Friedmann gives theoretical evidence that the universe expands
Lemaître proposes a linear distance and velocity relationship
beats.explain: Slipher's work came in 1912 to 1914, Friedmann's in 1922, Lemaître's in 1927 and Hubble's in 1929.

beats.prompt: Match each scientist to their contribution.
pairs: Used Einstein's equations to show expansion
Proposed a linear distance and velocity link
Recalculated the universe's size, doubling it
beats.explain: Each contribution added a piece to the picture of an expanding universe.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: The speed-of-light limit applies to local reference frames.
Distant galaxies can recede at rates that limit does not cover.
So a galaxy receding faster than light breaks relativity.
So the limit and the expansion can both hold.
beats.explain: The limit does not restrict the recession rates of cosmologically distant objects, so nothing is broken.
